property_summary: After calling transfer, the function reverts when _tos.length > 0.
After calling transfer, the function does not always revert when _tos.length > 0.
transfer does not revert when called with valid inputs
When transferring with a valid caddress that implements transferFrom, the transfer function returns true and does not revert.
The transfer function always returns true and does not revert when called with at least one recipient address.
After transfer() returns, the balance of any address in _tos should be greater than or equal to its balance before the call if _tos.length > 0
After calling transfer(from, caddress, _tos, v), the function returns true.
After calling transfer, the balance of each address in _tos is unchanged when caddress == address(c).
The transfer function returns true exactly once for each entry in _tos, as reflected by callcount tracking.
After transfer() returns, the gas used by the call is less than the block gas limit, and the function always returns true.
After calling transfer with the same parameters, the balances of the involved addresses remain unchanged.
The transfer function always returns true regardless of the operation outcome.
After calling transfer, the ether balance of caddress remains unchanged because the low-level call does not transfer any ether.
The function selector does not match the standard ERC20 transferFrom signature, so the nested call returns false but the outer transfer still succeeds.
After calling transfer, the return value of the low-level call does not matter for the outer function's return value.
All recipients in _tos array receive a transfer of the corresponding value v[i] from address.
The number of external calls made via caddress.call in transfer equals the number of recipients in _tos.
The total number of transfers executed equals the length of the _tos array.
The transfer function iterates over all elements in the _tos array.
The transfer function sends the correct amount of value to the last recipient in the array.
